messages:
alex: Customer hit ImportError immediately after pip installing our Python SDK (redwood==0.14.2) into what they thought was a venv. They say it imports fine from an interactive REPL but their app (gunicorn) fails with ModuleNotFoundError. Traceback pasted below:

alex: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/server.py", line 3, in <module>
    from redwood import RedwoodClient
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'

alex: They installed with: `pip install redwood-sdk[client]` on macOS. Reported pip --version and python -V outputs: 

alex: `pip --version` -> pip 23.1.2 from /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages (python 3.9)
alex: `python -V` -> Python 3.11.4

alex: Asking: is this likely a pip/pyenv/venv mismatch or an extras/dep not installing? Any quick repro steps to give the customer?

morgan: sounds like the classic pip vs python mismatch — pip is pointing at a different interpreter than the one running the app. Often happens with pyenv shims or when `pip` maps to system python.
morgan: Quick checks: share output of `which pip`, `which python`, `python -m pip show redwood-sdk`, and `python -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"`

alex: customer sent diagnostics: 

alex: `which pip` -> /usr/local/bin/pip
alex: `which python` -> /Users/runner/.pyenv/shims/python
alex: `python -m pip show redwood-sdk` -> WARNING: Package(s) not found: redwood-sdk

morgan: yep, pip and python disagree. The pip that installed the package put it into /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages, while the pyenv shim python is 3.11 and doesn't see that location.
morgan: Recommended fix: reinstall using the exact python used by the app: `python -m pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall "redwood-sdk[client]"`

jane: also check for stray .pth or sitecustomize that manipulates sys.path — in a few customer cases a leftover sitecustomize from a previous tool pointed sys.path at the wrong site-packages. Quick check: `python -c "import site, pprint; pprint.pprint(site.getsitepackages())"`

jane: if they run under gunicorn/uwsgi, ensure the same python binary is used by the service. systemd/unit files sometimes call a different interpreter (or rely on PATH).

alex: customer tried `python -m pip install redwood-sdk[client]` and got success message but import still fails in gunicorn.

sam: maybe gunicorn process uses a different virtualenv. Ask them to run inside the running process: `ps aux | grep gunicorn` and inspect the command line/venv path. Also test with `sudo -u someuser /path/to/python -c "import importlib.util; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"` to see if the interpreter that runs the service can find the package.

morgan: utility commands to send to customer (one-liners):

morgan: ```
# show where pip will install for the interpreter the app uses
/path/to/app/python -m pip --version
/path/to/app/python -m pip show redwood-sdk || echo "not installed for this python"
/path/to/app/python -c "import importlib.util, sys; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"
```

alex: customer returned with `importlib.util.find_spec('redwood')` -> None when run via the gunicorn python, but `find_spec` returns a value when run with their local dev python.

jane: okay that's conclusive — service's python doesn't have the package. Two common routes: 1) reinstall into the service's interpreter as discussed, or 2) update the service to point to the intended venv/python.
jane: if they prefer to avoid touching the service env, they can vendor the sdk into their app (not ideal) or fix the deployment script to use `python -m pip install` during build.

morgan: additional gotcha we saw before: if they used `--user` flag, packages end up in a user site dir which may not be visible to a system service. Check `python -m site --user-site` and see if redwood ended up there.

alex: customer also mentioned they installed with a symlinked python binary in CI which hid the mismatch. They ran `brew link` recently.

sam: final troubleshooting steps we gave them:

sam: 1) stop service, `python -m pip uninstall redwood-sdk redwood` (repeat until nothing found)
sam: 2) verify there are no leftover `redwood*` dirs in any site-packages paths: `python -c "import site, os; print([p for p in site.getsitepackages() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(p, 'redwood'))])"`
sam: 3) `python -m pip install 'redwood-sdk[client]==0.14.2' --no-cache-dir`
sam: 4) restart service with same python and verify `python -c "import importlib.util; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"` from the service runtime

alex: customer followed those steps and confirmed import now works in the live service. :white_check_mark:

devx-bot: Suggestion: add a short blurb to our troubleshooting docs: "When imports fail in a deployed service but work in REPL, check pip vs python mismatch (pyenv/shims, system pip, --user installs) and verify the interpreter used by the process." Might save future tickets.

jane: +1 — I'll add a small note to the SDK troubleshooting doc and include the exact commands we used.

morgan: marking resolved, closing thread.
